leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, coriaceous (leathery), oblong-lanceolate leaves, copper-red when young turning dark lustrous green
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark glossy green

stem_characteristics: Stout, erect trunk with rough, dark grey-brown fissured bark and dense spreading dome canopy, 10–30 m
flower_characteristics: Terminal large branched panicles with thousands of tiny fragrant yellowish-pink flowers (hermaphrodite and male)
fruit_characteristics: Large fleshy drupe with prominent resinous stone (endocarp), yellow/orange/red skin with sweet juicy pulp
growth_habit: Large majestic evergreen canopy tree, 10–30 meters tall
habitat_and_climate: Tropical and sub-tropical climate; distinct dry period essential for profuse winter flowering
sunlight_requirements: Full blazing tropical sun (8+ hours daily)
water_requirements: Moderate; critical during fruit development; withhold before flowering
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained alluvial loams and fertile red loams, pH 5.5–7.5
growing_season: Spring flowering (Jan–March), summer harvest (April–July)
propagation_methods: Veneer grafting, epicotyl grafting, inarching
uses: King of fruits; eaten fresh (Alphonso, Banganapalli, Dasheri, Kesar, Langra)
Processed: mango pulp, aam papad, pickles, mango lassi
Mango wood for religious havans and timber
safety_notes: Mango sap / stem peel contains urushiol contact resin causing contact dermatitis in allergic individuals.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Dark brown tear-stain necrotic spots on foliage, blossom blight, and black rotting on ripening fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium mangiferae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth covering panicles causing total flower drop and fruit drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Dinocap (1 ml/L) at panicle emergence

prevention_guidance: Spray Paclobutrazol (Cultar) in soil basin in Sept-Oct to promote profuse flowering
Prune congested dead branches after post-harvest to allow sunlight into canopy

leaf_characteristics.shape: Gigantic oblong-elliptic smooth arching blades with prominent central midrib and lateral transverse parallel veins
leaf_characteristics.margin: Entire, tearing naturally along transverse veins in wind
leaf_characteristics.color: Bright lush green

stem_characteristics: Pseudostem formed by tightly packed overlapping concentric leaf sheaths, 2–6 m tall
flower_characteristics: Large terminal pendulous inflorescence with purple-red ovate bracts, female flowers at base, male bud (heart) at tip
fruit_characteristics: Elongated parthenocarpic fleshy berry (finger) in tiered clusters (hands) along central stalk (bunch)
growth_habit: Large arborescent perennial evergreen giant herb, 2–6 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm, humid tropical climate with high rainfall and temperature 22°C–35°C; highly sensitive to frost
water_requirements: High water requirement (1800–2200 mm); sensitive to drought stress
soil_preferences: Deep, rich, well-drained loamy to clay loam soils with high organic matter, pH 6.0–7.5
growing_season: Year-round planting and harvesting (Grand Naine, Robusta, Poovan, Nendran)
propagation_methods: Sword suckers (1.5–2.0 kg) or certified tissue culture plantlets
uses: Major fruit crop; fresh dessert fruit, baby food, chips, plantain curry
Flower heart (vazhaipoo) and pseudostem core (vazhaithandu) cooked as vegetables
Broad leaves used as traditional biodegradable dining plates across South India
safety_notes: Safe for consumption.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Panama Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaf margins, petiole buckling, vascular discoloration of pseudostem, plant collapse
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Plant resistant Grand Naine; dip suckers in Carbendazim (2 g/L); apply Trichoderma viride with FYM

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Sigatoka Leaf Spot (Pseudocercospora musae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped chlorotic streaks turning dark brown/black with light grey sunken centers
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Propiconazole (1 ml/L) mixed with mineral oil

prevention_guidance: De-suckering: retain only one follower sucker per clump to channel nutrients to main bunch
Bag developing bunch with perforated blue polyethylene sleeves to protect from sunburn and thrips

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, elliptic to oblong leathery leaves with prominent raised parallel veins beneath
leaf_characteristics.color: Dull medium green with aromatic glandular dots

stem_characteristics: Smooth, thin, peeling coppery-brown bark with green patches, quadrangular young twigs, 3–8 m
flower_characteristics: White solitary or 2–3 clustered flowers with numerous showy white stamens
fruit_characteristics: Globose to pyriform berry with persistent calyx, green skin ripening yellow, white or pink pulp with hard seeds
growth_habit: Small evergreen or semi-deciduous tree or spreading shrub, 3–8 meters
habitat_and_climate: Tropical and sub-tropical climate; highly adaptable and drought hardy
water_requirements: Moderate; drought tolerant once established
soil_preferences: Tolerates varied soils: alluvial loams, clay loams, red soils; withstands soil salinity and pH 4.5–8.2
growing_season: Two main crops: Mrig Bahar (winter fruiting, superior quality) and Ambe Bahar (monsoon fruiting)
propagation_methods: Air layering (guttee), wedge grafting, or budding (Lucknow 49 / Sardar, Allahabad Safeda)
uses: High-vitamin C fruit (4 times higher than orange); eaten fresh with chaat masala
Jams, jellies (high natural pectin content), guava nectar
Tender leaves boiled for mouth ulcers and gastrointestinal soothing
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Guava Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. psidii)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Rapid yellowing and browning of leaves, twig die-back, complete wilting of mature tree
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Drench basin with Carbendazim (2 g/L); graft on resistant Psidium cattleianum rootstock

prevention_guidance: Withhold irrigation in summer to force winter Mrig Bahar crop
Fruit bagging with foam nets protects from fruit flies

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large, palmately 7–11 deeply lobed leaves (50–70 cm across) with hollow cylindrical petioles (1 m)
leaf_characteristics.color: Vibrant light green to dark green

stem_characteristics: Soft-wooded, erect, hollow unbranched single cylindrical trunk with prominent leaf scars, 2–8 m
flower_characteristics: Polygamous (dioecious, gynodioecious, hermaphrodite): waxy creamy-white to yellow fragrant tubular flowers
fruit_characteristics: Large cylindrical to globose berry (0.5–3.0 kg), orange-yellow skin, salmon-orange flesh with gelatinous black seeds
growth_habit: Fast-growing soft-wooded herbaceous tree-like perennial, 2–8 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm tropical climate; completely intolerant of frost and waterlogging
water_requirements: Regular moderate moisture; collar region must stay dry to prevent stem rot
soil_preferences: Deep, fertile, well-drained rich sandy loam with high organic matter, pH 6.0–7.0
growing_season: Year-round fruiting (Red Lady 786, Pusa Delicious, Coorg Honey Dew)
propagation_methods: Seed sowing in nursery polybags
uses: Sweet dessert fruit rich in beta-carotene and Vitamin C
Raw green papaya cooked in curries (som tam, chutney)
Latex source of papain enzyme for meat tenderizing and digestive therapeutics
safety_notes: Unripe green papaya latex contains papain enzyme; pregnant women are advised to avoid raw unpeeled papaya.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Yellow mosaic mottling on leaves, shoestring distortion, water-soaked oily rings on stems and fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Vector aphid control with systemic insecticides; rogue infected trees immediately

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Foot Rot / Stem Rot (Pythium aphanidermatum)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked soft rotting at soil collar level causing tree toppling
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Ensure elevated mound planting; drench collar with Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L)

prevention_guidance: Plant on 20 cm raised mounds to ensure water never pools around stem collar
Maintain 1 male tree for every 10 female trees in dioecious orchards

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large pinnately divided feather-like arching fronds (4–6 m long) with numerous linear-lanceolate rigid leaflets
leaf_characteristics.color: Lustrous emerald green to golden green

stem_characteristics: Tall, slender, unbranched cylindrical ringed trunk with swollen base and adventitious root bole, 15–30 m
flower_characteristics: Monoecious: spadix inflorescence enclosed in woody spathe; male flowers numerous at tip, female button flowers at base
fruit_characteristics: Large fibrous 3-sided ovoid drupe with smooth exocarp, thick fibrous coir mesocarp, hard stony endocarp, and sweet liquid/solid endosperm
growth_habit: Tall majestic single-stemmed evergreen palm tree, 15–30 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm humid tropical maritime coastal belt and river basins; frost-free
water_requirements: High (40–50 liters/palm/day in summer); responds to coastal saltwater and brackish aquifers
soil_preferences: Deep coastal sandy soils, alluvial loams, and red laterites with good percolation, pH 5.2–8.0
growing_season: Perennial continuous fruiting (West Coast Tall, East Coast Tall, Chowghat Orange Dwarf, DXT hybrids)
propagation_methods: Selected mature seed coconut germination
uses: Kalpavriksha (tree of heaven): tender coconut water (natural electrolyte), coconut oil, copra, grated coconut in food
Coir fiber for ropes, geotextiles, mattresses, and coir pith compost
Leaves for thatch, trunk for building timber
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Rhinoceros Beetle (Oryctes rhinoceros)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Geometric V-shaped geometric cuts on emerging fronds; chewing into cabbage crown
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Hook out beetles from crown; pack top leaf axils with sevidol/sand mixture (1:1)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Root (Wilt) Disease
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Flaccidity and abnormal inward ribbing of leaflets, marginal necrosis, yellowing
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Balanced NPK + Magnesium Sulfate (500 g/palm); intercrop with green manure

prevention_guidance: Apply 1 kg urea, 2 kg single superphosphate, and 2 kg muriate of potash per mature palm annually
Practice basin mulching with coconut leaves and coir pith

leaf_characteristics.shape: Pinnately divided arching fronds (1.5–2 m) crowded at stem crown with lanceolate clustered pinnae
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark glossy green

stem_characteristics: Slender, perfectly straight erect annulated trunk (15–20 cm diameter) with distinct pale nodal rings, 12–25 m
flower_characteristics: Spadix inflorescence branching under crownshaft; small fragrant white male flowers and fewer female flowers
fruit_characteristics: Fibrous ovoid to globose drupe (4–6 cm), bright orange-red when ripe, enclosing hard ruminate seed (nut)
growth_habit: Slender tall single-stemmed evergreen feather palm, 12–25 meters
habitat_and_climate: Humid tropical rainforest zones and foothills (Western Ghats and Northeast India); sensitive to drought and sunscald
sunlight_requirements: Partial shade when young; filtered to full sun as canopy matures
water_requirements: High regular moisture; sensitive to water deficit
soil_preferences: Deep fertile lateritic loams and clay loams rich in organic matter with excellent drainage, pH 5.5–6.5
growing_season: Perennial fruiting (Mangala, Sumangala, Mohitnagar, South Kanara)
propagation_methods: Ripe seed nut nursery germination
uses: Betel nut chewed with paan (piper betle leaf and slaked lime)
Tannins for dyeing and leather tanning
Areca leaf sheaths pressed into eco-friendly biodegradable plates and bowls
safety_notes: Habitual chewing of areca nut with tobacco is clinically proven to cause oral submucous fibrosis and oral carcinomas.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Koleroga / Fruit Rot (Phytophthora meadii)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on nuts causing heavy premature rotting and dropping of green nuts during monsoon
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Prophylactic spraying of 1% Bordeaux mixture before monsoon onset; cover bunches with polythene bags

prevention_guidance: Tie polyethylene bags over developing nut bunches before heavy monsoon to prevent Koleroga
Intercrop with Pepper, Banana, and Cocoa

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, coriaceous (leathery), elliptic to obovate glossy dark green leaves
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark glossy green above, paler beneath

stem_characteristics: Stout, straight trunk with rough dark grey-brown bark; exhibits cauliflory (flowers directly on trunk and older boughs), 10–20 m
flower_characteristics: Monoecious: cylindrical fleshy spikes; male spikes on younger twigs, female spikes directly on main trunk and thick branches
fruit_characteristics: World's largest tree-borne fruit: giant syncarp (10–35 kg) with spiny pyramidal rind holding golden-yellow aromatic bulbs (arils)
growth_habit: Large stately evergreen canopy tree, 10–20 meters
habitat_and_climate: Humid tropical Western Ghats and Northeast rainforests; warm and frost-free
water_requirements: Moderate; deep taproot system withstands dry periods
soil_preferences: Deep, fertile, well-drained alluvial and lateritic sandy loams; strictly avoids waterlogged roots
growing_season: Summer fruiting (March–July)
propagation_methods: Seeds (fresh), approach grafting, air layering
uses: Raw tender green jackfruit cooked as vegetarian 'plant meat' curry (kathal sabzi)
Ripe golden bulbs eaten fresh, halwa, chips, ice cream
Nutritious seeds boiled or roasted
Valuable yellow timber for furniture and musical instruments
safety_notes: Latex sap is very sticky; grease hands and knives with coconut oil before cutting.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Rhizopus Fruit Rot (Rhizopus artocarpi)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Soft watery black rot on male inflorescences and young fruitlets covered in greyish-black whisker mycelium
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) or Mancozeb

prevention_guidance: Prune dead wood and water sprouts to keep main trunk clean for cauliflorous fruit emergence

leaf_characteristics.shape: Narrow, oblong-lanceolate smooth glossy leaves with short reddish petiole
leaf_characteristics.arrangement: Opposite or clustered on spur twigs
leaf_characteristics.color: Lustrous bright green

stem_characteristics: Multi-stemmed spiny spreading shrub or small tree with grey bark, 3–6 m
flower_characteristics: Showy solitary or clustered bright scarlet-red tubular flowers with fleshy calyx
fruit_characteristics: Globose berry (balausta) with tough leathery red/yellow rind and persistent crown calyx, interior filled with ruby-red juicy arils
growth_habit: Deciduous spiny spreading shrub or small tree, 3–6 meters
habitat_and_climate: Semi-arid sub-tropical to tropical climate with dry hot summers and cool winters
water_requirements: Moderate; highly drought hardy, but uniform drip irrigation prevents fruit cracking
soil_preferences: Well-drained light loamy soils to medium black soils, pH 6.5–8.0
growing_season: Mrig Bahar (monsoon flower, winter harvest) and Hastha Bahar (Bhagwa / Sindhuri / Ganesh)
propagation_methods: Air layering, hardwood cuttings, or tissue culture
uses: Nutrient-dense superfruit rich in punicalagins, ellagic acid, and antioxidants
Fresh arils, pure juice, anardana (dried sour seeds as spice)
Rind used in Ayurvedic remedies for diarrhea
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Bacterial Blight / Telya (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. punicae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked angular black spots on leaves, black cankers on twigs, Y-shaped or L-shaped black oily cracks on fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Strict sanitation; prune infected twigs; spray Streptocycline (0.5 g/L) + Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Fruit Borer / Anar Butterfly (Deudorix isocrates)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Caterpillar bores inside developing fruit, causing rotting and fruit drop with foul frass
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Bag young fruits with butter paper/cloth bags at marble stage; spray Chlorantraniliprole

prevention_guidance: Bag young developing fruits (5 cm diameter) with butter paper bags to prevent 100% insect and sunscald damage
Adopt drip irrigation to avoid wet foliage

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large, cordate palmately 3–5 lobed leaves with coarsely serrate margins
leaf_characteristics.color: Rich green with distinct veins

stem_characteristics: Woody climbing deciduous vine with leaf-opposed branched coiled tendrils, up to 15 m
flower_characteristics: Dense panicles of tiny yellowish-green fragrant flowers
fruit_characteristics: Globose to ellipsoid fleshy juicy berries in tight pendulous bunches (green, purple, red, black)
growth_habit: Vigorous woody perennial climbing liana, trained on overhead pandals, 3–15 m
habitat_and_climate: Warm dry Mediterranean to subtropical climate; dry rainless sunny weather during berry ripening is essential
water_requirements: Controlled drip irrigation; withholding water before harvest enhances Brix sugars
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained sandy loam or gravelly loam soils, pH 6.5–7.8
growing_season: Double pruning system: Foundation pruning (April) and Forward fruiting pruning (October)
propagation_methods: Hardwood cuttings grafted on Dog Ridge rootstock (Thomson Seedless, Sonaka, Sharad Seedless)
uses: Fresh table fruit, sweet raisins (kishmish), premium wine production
Grape seed oil and resveratrol antioxidant extract
safety_notes: Safe for human consumption. TOXIC to dogs (causes acute kidney failure).

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Downy Mildew (Plasmopara viticola)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Yellowish translucent 'oil spots' on upper leaf surface with dense white cottony fungal growth on underside
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Uncinula necator)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Ash-grey powdery coating on leaves and young berries causing berry cracking
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar sulfur dust or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L)

prevention_guidance: Train on Bower / Pergola trellises for optimal airflow and sunlight interception
Dip developing bunches in Gibberellic Acid (GA3 @ 10–40 ppm) for berry elongation

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple elliptic-ovate coriaceous leaves with narrowly winged petiole and citrus aroma
leaf_characteristics.color: Glossy dark green with translucent oil glands

stem_characteristics: Spreading thorny shrub or small tree with sharp axillary spines, 3–6 m
flower_characteristics: Fragrant solitary or clustered white flowers with purplish-tinted exterior petals
fruit_characteristics: Ovoid to ellipsoid hesperidium with distinct terminal nipple, yellow rind, and sour acidic juice
growth_habit: Small evergreen thorny tree or spreading shrub, 3–6 meters
habitat_and_climate: Sub-tropical and tropical climate; frost sensitive
water_requirements: Regular moderate watering; avoids soggy root zones
soil_preferences: Well-drained light loamy soils to medium black soils, pH 6.0–7.5
growing_season: Year-round flowering and fruiting with major flushes (Kagzi, Baramasi, Eureka)

uses: Universal culinary souring agent, fresh nimbu pani (lemonade), pickles
Rich source of Vitamin C and citric acid; preservation and cleansing
safety_notes: Plant has sharp axillary thorns. Peel contains photosensitizing psoralen oils.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas citri)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Raised, corky, rough brownish pustules surrounded by yellow chlorotic halo on leaves, twigs, and fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Prune cankered twigs; spray Streptocycline (100 ppm) + Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Citrus Leaf Miner (Phyllocnistis citrella)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Silvery serpentine zigzag mines on tender young leaves causing severe leaf curling
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 ml/L) or Neem oil (5 ml/L)

prevention_guidance: Prune interior water shoots and cross branches annually
Paint trunk base with Bordeaux paste to prevent gummosis

leaf_characteristics.color: Bright shiny green

stem_characteristics: Dense bushy spreading thorny shrub or small tree with short stiff sharp spines, 2–4 m
flower_characteristics: Small pure white fragrant flowers in axillary clusters of 2–7
fruit_characteristics: Small globose to sub-globose thin-skinned hesperidium (3–5 cm), greenish-yellow with intensely sour juice

common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Corky eruptive spots on foliage and lime fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Streptocycline + Copper Oxychloride

Maintain good drainage to prevent phytophthora gummosis

leaf_characteristics.color: Dark glossy green

stem_characteristics: Medium-sized compact evergreen tree with rounded canopy and slender thorns, 4–8 m
flower_characteristics: Intensely fragrant solitary or clustered pure white waxy flowers
fruit_characteristics: Globose hesperidium with smooth green to golden-yellow rind, sweet mild juice with low acidity
growth_habit: Compact evergreen rounded fruit tree, 4–8 meters
habitat_and_climate: Subtropical to tropical climate with dry winter and warm sunny summers
water_requirements: Moderate regular drip irrigation
soil_preferences: Well-drained deep loamy and black soils with good aeration, pH 6.5–7.5
growing_season: Ambe Bahar (Feb–March flower, Nov–Dec harvest) and Mrig Bahar
propagation_methods: T-budding on Rangpur Lime or Jatti Khatti rootstock
uses: India's most popular fresh juice fruit (sweet mosambi juice, rich in Vitamin C and potassium)
Table fruit and therapeutic rehydration for convalescents
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Die-back / Gummosis (Phytophthora nicotianae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Gum exudation from trunk base, bark splitting, yellowing and dying back of twigs
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Scrape gummed bark; apply Bordeaux paste; drench with Fosetyl-Al (2 g/L)

prevention_guidance: Bud on Phytophthora-tolerant Rangpur Lime rootstock
Keep graft union at least 25 cm above ground level

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, coriaceous (leathery), elliptic-lanceolate glossy dark green leaves crowded at twig ends
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark lustrous green with prominent veins

stem_characteristics: Stout, erect trunk with dark grey-brown rough fissured bark and horizontal branching, 8–15 m
flower_characteristics: Small, bell-shaped solitary white or pale cream flowers on rusty-hairy pedicels in leaf axils
fruit_characteristics: Globose to ovoid fleshy berry with rough scurfy brown rind; sweet, brown, granular, honey-sweet pulp with shiny black seeds
growth_habit: Medium to large evergreen rounded tree, 8–15 meters tall
habitat_and_climate: Warm humid tropical coastal climate; withstands coastal saline sea breezes and windstorms
water_requirements: Moderate; highly drought hardy once mature
soil_preferences: Tolerates varied soils: coastal alluvium, sandy loams, deep black soils, and laterites, pH 6.0–8.0
growing_season: Continuous year-round fruiting with two peak harvest seasons (Kalipatti, Cricket Ball, PKM-1)
propagation_methods: Approach grafting (inarching) or softwood grafting on Khirni (Manilkara hexandra) rootstock
uses: Popular sweet table fruit (chikoo shakes, ice creams, halwa)
Natural source of sugars (fructose/sucrose) and dietary fiber
Traditional source of chicle latex used in chewing gum
safety_notes: Seeds have an apical hook that can catch in the throat if swallowed whole. Discard seeds.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Leaf Spot (Phaeophleospora indica)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Small circular brown spots with whitish centers on leaves causing defoliation
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Bud Borer (Anarsia achrasella)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Caterpillar webs together buds and tender leaves, boring into flower buds
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Quinalphos or Chlorpyrifos

prevention_guidance: Graft on hardy Khirni (Manilkara hexandra) rootstock for lifelong vigor
Harvest mature fruits when brown scurf rubs off easily and skin shows yellowish-green tinge underneath

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, oblong-lanceolate smooth thin leaves with distinct aromatic odor when crushed
leaf_characteristics.color: Dull blue-green above, paler glaucous beneath

stem_characteristics: Slender, branched small deciduous tree or large shrub with thin grey bark, 3–6 m
flower_characteristics: Solitary or clustered greenish-yellow drooping fleshy 3-petaled flowers with numerous stamens
fruit_characteristics: Globose to heart-shaped tuberculate syncarp with prominent rounded polygonal knobs/segments (carpels); creamy sweet white pulp with glossy black seeds
growth_habit: Small deciduous tree or sprawling shrub, 3–6 meters
habitat_and_climate: Tropical and sub-tropical semi-arid climate; exceptionally drought hardy and heat tolerant
water_requirements: Low water requirement; survives in rainfed rocky terrain
soil_preferences: Rocky, gravelly, shallow soils, light sandy loams, and red soils, pH 6.0–7.5
growing_season: Autumn harvest (September–November) (Balanagar, Arka Sahan, NMK-1 Golden)
propagation_methods: Seeds, wedge grafting, or budding on seedling rootstocks

Seeds contain insecticidal acetogenins traditionally used against lice and crop pests
safety_notes: CRITICAL NOTE: Seeds are toxic and should not be crushed or chewed. Do not consume seeds.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Mealybug (Maconellicoccus hirsutus)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White waxy colonies clustered in grooves between fruit segments, producing sooty mold
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Release Cryptolaemus montrouzieri ladybird predator; spray Buprofezin (1 ml/L) or Neem oil

prevention_guidance: Hand pollination in morning hours increases fruit set by 60% and eliminates lopsided fruits

leaf_characteristics.shape: Small, linear-oblong, closely spaced pinnately arranged leaves on deciduous branchlets resembling compound leaves
leaf_characteristics.color: Light fresh green

stem_characteristics: Small to medium deciduous tree with flaking greenish-grey bark revealing pinkish underbark, 6–12 m
flower_characteristics: Small, inconspicuous greenish-yellow flowers in compact axillary clusters on lower branchlets
fruit_characteristics: Depressed globose 6-lobed smooth fleshy berry (2–4 cm), pale yellow-green with 6-ribbed hard stone
growth_habit: Small to medium deciduous tree, 6–12 meters
habitat_and_climate: Sub-tropical and tropical semi-arid zones; highly drought hardy and tolerant of light frost
water_requirements: Low to moderate; withstands long dry spells
soil_preferences: Highly versatile: thrives in sodic/alkaline soils (pH up to 9.0), gravelly red soils, and alluvium
growing_season: Winter harvest (November–February) (NA-7, Chakaiya, Kanchan, Banarasi, Krishna)
propagation_methods: Patch budding or shield budding on wild seedling rootstocks
uses: Premier Ayurvedic rasayana (rejuvenator); primary ingredient in Chyawanprash and Triphala
Richest natural source of Vitamin C (600–900 mg/100g, stabilized by tannins)
Amla murabba, candy, pickles, hair oil, digestive supari
safety_notes: Extremely safe and revered in traditional and modern nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Amla Rust (Ravenelia emblicae)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Ring of brownish pustules on leaflets and circular black spots on fruits
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Mancozeb

prevention_guidance: Prune dead branches and thin crowded shoots annually after harvest
Mulch tree basin with paddy straw to conserve moisture

leaf_characteristics.color: Fresh pale to medium green

stem_characteristics: Massive, imposing trunk with rough dark grey fissured bark and dense spreading rounded dome canopy, 12–25 m
flower_characteristics: Small pale yellow 5-petaled flowers with reddish-orange veins in drooping racemes
fruit_characteristics: Cinnamon-brown indehiscent curved pendulous pod with brittle shell, thick sour-sweet tart pulp, and glossy brown seeds
growth_habit: Large, long-lived stately evergreen tree living over 200 years, 12–25 meters
habitat_and_climate: Semi-arid tropical and subtropical plains; exceptionally drought and wind resistant
water_requirements: Low; rainfed once established
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained loams, gravelly red soils, and riverbanks; tolerates salinity and pH 5.5–8.5

propagation_methods: Grafting, air layering, or seed

High in natural tartaric acid, potassium, and pectin
Valuable hard timber and shade avenue tree
safety_notes: Safe for culinary consumption.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal spots on tender leaves
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Sulfur spray

prevention_guidance: Plant along field boundaries and road avenues as living windbreaks

leaf_characteristics.shape: Opposite, coriaceous (leathery), oblong-elliptic glossy dark green leaves with faint turpentine aroma
leaf_characteristics.venation: Pinnate with numerous fine parallel lateral veins
leaf_characteristics.color: Lustrous dark green above, paler beneath

stem_characteristics: Stout, majestic trunk with rough light grey-brown exfoliating bark and dense spreading canopy, 10–25 m
flower_characteristics: Small, fragrant greenish-white flowers in branched cymes on older twigs
fruit_characteristics: Oblong-ellipsoid fleshy berry (2–4 cm), green ripening to lustrous deep purple-black with pink-purple staining astringent-sweet juice
growth_habit: Large handsome evergreen canopy tree, 10–25 meters
habitat_and_climate: Tropical and sub-tropical plains, riverine tracts, and moist depressions; tolerates waterlogging

Seed powder widely used in Ayurveda for managing type 2 diabetes mellitus
Water-resistant timber traditionally used for well linings

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Anthracnose
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Leaf spots and fruit rot
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Copper oxychloride spray

prevention_guidance: Pick fruits manually when fully purple-black; fallen fruits bruise easily

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large, deeply pinnatifid 3–5 lobed leaves with undulating round-tipped lobes and rough hairs
leaf_characteristics.color: Greyish green with scabrid pubescence

stem_characteristics: Trailing angular hairy grooved vine with 2–3 branched coiled tendrils, 2–4 m
flower_characteristics: Solitary pale yellow 5-petaled flowers; female flowers have hairy inferior ovary
fruit_characteristics: Large globose to oblong smooth pepo (3–12 kg) with green striped rind, deep crimson-red sugary pulp (92% water) and flat black seeds
growth_habit: Annual trailing herbaceous sprawling vine, 2–4 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm, dry, sunny summer climate; requires hot days (28°C–35°C) and cool nights for high sugar accumulation
water_requirements: Regular uniform irrigation; stop watering 7–10 days before harvest to build sweetness
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained sandy riverbeds and sandy loam soils, pH 6.0–7.0
growing_season: Summer (Zaid) season (January–April in riverbeds)

uses: India's premier summer hydrating fruit; rich in lycopene, citrulline, and electrolytes
Seeds roasted as nutritious protein-rich snack
safety_notes: Safe for human diet.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. niveum)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Unilateral wilting of runner vines, vascular browning, sudden collapse
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Crop rotation with non-cucurbits; seed treatment with Trichoderma (5 g/kg)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Downy Mildew
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Angular yellow patches on foliage
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Metalaxyl spray

prevention_guidance: Riverbed 'Diara' cultivation utilizes natural subsoil moisture in dry sandy river courses
Tap fruit: dull hollow thumping sound indicates full ripeness

leaf_characteristics.shape: Sub-orbicular to reniform shallowly 3–5 angled cordate leaves with soft rough hairs
leaf_characteristics.color: Fresh green with rough hispid hairs

stem_characteristics: Sprawling grooved hairy vine with simple unbranched tendrils, 1.5–3.0 m
flower_characteristics: Small yellow bell-shaped flowers in leaf axils
fruit_characteristics: Globose to oval fragrant pepo with netted (reticulate) or smooth ribbed rind; sweet orange or green flesh with central cavity of seeds
growth_habit: Annual sprawling trailing vine, 1.5–3.0 meters
habitat_and_climate: Hot, dry sunny summer climate; high humidity invites foliar diseases and reduces sugar content
water_requirements: Moderate; avoid wetting developing fruits directly
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained sandy loams and river sand beds, pH 6.0–7.5
growing_season: Summer (Zaid) (February–May)
propagation_methods: Direct pit sowing on mounds
uses: Aromatic sweet summer fruit; cooling, rich in beta-carotene and potassium
Seeds dried and ground in traditional cooling thandai drink
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on foliage
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Wettable sulfur or Azoxystrobin spray

prevention_guidance: Harvest at 'half-slip' to 'full-slip' stage when fruit easily detaches from vine with slight thumb pressure

leaf_characteristics.shape: Rosette of 30–50 sword-shaped rigid waxy trough-like leaves with sharp marginal spines and pointed tip
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark glossy green with reddish or silvery glaucous underside

stem_characteristics: Short, stout fleshy unbranched stem terminating in central composite flower head, 0.8–1.2 m
flower_characteristics: Compact dense cylindrical spike of 50–200 purplish-blue flowers topped by a crown of small leaves
fruit_characteristics: Large cylindrical multiple fruit (syncarp, 1–2.5 kg) formed by fusion of berrylets around fibrous central core; crowned by leafy top
growth_habit: Terrestrial evergreen perennial bromeliad herb, 0.8–1.2 meters
habitat_and_climate: Warm, humid tropical climate with high rainfall; sensitive to frost and waterlogging
water_requirements: Moderate; trough leaves channel dew and rain directly into stem core
soil_preferences: Well-drained light sandy loam and acidic lateritic soils, pH 4.5–5.5
growing_season: Year-round fruiting with chemical induction (Giant Kew, Queen, Mauritius)
propagation_methods: Slips, suckers, or fruit crowns
uses: Sweet-tart tropical fruit eaten fresh, canned slices, juice
Contains bromelain proteolytic enzyme used for tenderizing and anti-inflammatory therapy
Piña fiber extracted from leaves for textiles
safety_notes: Contains bromelain enzyme which may cause mild tingling sensation on tongue.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Heart Rot (Phytophthora cinnamomi)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Heart leaves turn yellow, pull out easily from stem base with foul rotting odor
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Ensure elevated bed drainage; dip suckers in Metalaxyl (2 g/L) before planting

prevention_guidance: Spray Ethephon (100 ppm) into heart of 35-leaf plants to trigger synchronized flowering across orchard

common_name: Indian Jujube / Ber / Poor Man's Apple

leaf_characteristics.shape: Small, ovate to elliptic glossy dark green leaves, densely covered with white/buff felted tomentum beneath
leaf_characteristics.color: Glossy dark green above, whitish woolly beneath

stem_characteristics: Spreading thorny shrub or small tree with zigzag branchlets and sharp paired stipular spines (one straight, one hooked), 4–10 m
flower_characteristics: Small inconspicuous greenish-yellow fragrant flowers in axillary cymes
fruit_characteristics: Globose to oblong fleshy drupe (2–5 cm) with smooth shiny skin, green turning golden-yellow to reddish-brown; sweet-sour pulp with hard stone
growth_habit: Extremely hardy spiny evergreen or semi-deciduous tree, 4–10 meters
habitat_and_climate: Arid and semi-arid desert climate; extreme drought hardiness and heat tolerance (up to 48°C)
water_requirements: Very low; survives where other fruit trees fail
soil_preferences: Tolerates poor soils: sandy, gravelly, saline, and alkaline soils, pH 6.5–9.0
growing_season: Winter harvest (December–March) (Gola, Seb, Umran, Kaithli, Apple Ber)
propagation_methods: Ring budding or shield budding on wild Ziziphus rotundifolia rootstock
uses: Poor man's apple: eaten fresh, dried, candies, and pickles
Valuable source of Vitamin C and minerals in desert ecosystems
Host plant for lac insects (Kerria lacca) and silkworms; dry spiny branches for livestock fencing
safety_notes: Sharp paired hooked spines require careful manual picking. Safe.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium erysiphoides f. sp. ziziphi)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on developing fruits causing skin corking and fruit drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Dinocap during marble stage

prevention_guidance: Annual severe pruning in May–June is essential to stimulate vigorous new fruiting wood for winter crop
